definition: A theoretical framework that predicts stable multi-shell icosahedral structures by optimizing size mismatch between adjacent shells categorized by chiral type
assumptions: Atoms can be treated as hard spheres with well-defined radii
Shells are constructed on a hexagonal lattice projected onto an icosahedron
Size mismatch is the primary determinant of shell stability
Lennard-Jones potentials adequately describe interatomic interactions
Growth proceeds via sequential shell addition
invariants: Icosahedral symmetry (I or I_h) is preserved
Shell atom counts follow magic number sequences
Chiral categories are discrete (MC, BG, Ch1-Ch5)
Size mismatch is computed as |r_outer - r_inner| / r_inner
non_negotiable_steps: Compute Mackay magic numbers from formula N_k = (10k^3 - 15k^2 + 11k - 3)/3
Determine chiral category for each shell based on hexagonal lattice path
Calculate size mismatch for candidate element pairs
Compare mismatch against optimal ranges for relevant transition type
